A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SupervisorAgent research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, cross-model and cross-framework experiments, and a GAIA case study.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds full-validation-set ablations, threshold sensitivity, token-overhead breakdowns and latency measurements.

M1.justification: The core supervision strategies, context and action space, intervention pipeline and supplied prompts are retained. The new pseudocode, framework-specific integration descriptions and guidance cap expand documentation of the existing system; the PDFs do not establish an actual implementation change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GAIA, GSM8k-Hard, AIME 2024, HumanEval, MBPP and DROP. The added analyses use existing GAIA coverage; extending ablations from selected tasks to the full validation set changes sampling scope rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1, 2 and 4 is unchanged, including the AWorld variants with and without Guard. The expanded ablation retains the same three component-removal variants; token-accounting rows do not introduce new comparison methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds component ablations on the full GAIA validation set alongside the original top-10-token-intensive-tasks-per-level evaluation. It also introduces a purification-threshold sweep over 1000, 3000, 5000 and 7000 characters and latency evaluation in seconds. These substantially expand the evaluation design; existing headline benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's selected-subset ablation, v2 tests component contributions across the full validation set, sensitivity to purification thresholds, supervisor token overhead and each component's latency cost. The original subset ablation survives as Table 8, and the existing case study moves from A.4 to A.6.

E5.justification: The pass@k reporting and token-cost distribution/variance analysis are retained. v2 introduces no seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or statistical tests; its added experiments report point estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results in Table 3, Figure 5 and Tables 6–7. For example, full-set accuracy is 49.70% without purification versus 50.91% with the full system, while average latency is 233.96 seconds for Smolagent versus 321.15 seconds for SMAS. Tables 1, 2 and 4 remain numerically unchanged, and Table 8 reproduces v1's Table 3; the new ablation values concern different sample coverage, not cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The SMAS and context-window definitions and context-dependent action space are unchanged. Algorithm 1 documents operational heuristics without adding theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract corrects the claimed GAIA token saving from 29.45% to 29.68%, aligning it with Table 1 and the conclusion already present in v1. The central runtime-supervision, efficiency and general-applicability contributions retain their scope.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly interprets the token–latency tradeoff and attributes most latency overhead to purification. Appendix A.5 adds specific limitations involving very long observations, ineffective guidance and backbone-dependent trigger frequency. These substantially extend v1's more general discussion of overcompression and resource accounting.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Table 5 disclose filter logic and benchmark-specific step intervals and loop windows. Appendix A.3.2 adds OAgents settings and AWorld's MCP invocation/routing details, while A.5 specifies a maximum of two guidance interventions per subtask. These materially expand reproducibility information; the supplied prompts and code-access URL are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning against post-hoc failure attribution, architectural optimization and AWorld's Guard are retained. Changes to Gao's author name and the MaAS reference are bibliographic corrections rather than new research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and affiliation/header edits, merges Discussion and Conclusion, and adds acknowledgements, ethics and reproducibility statements. It inserts new appendix sections and renumbers the retained case study and prompts, while preserving most original prose and all supplied prompt content.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual presentation with Figures 5–7, Tables 5–7 and Algorithm 1. It redraws Figure 4a for the full-set ablation, presents those results in Table 3, and relocates the original subset table to Table 8. These are substantive display additions and revisions beyond pagination changes.

improvement.justification: v1's component evidence was limited to selected high-cost tasks and lacked latency measurements. v2 adds full-set ablations, sensitivity testing and important implementation details, substantially strengthening validation and reproducibility. Reporting the 37.27% latency increase makes the retained token savings more honestly assessable. Although A.4.1 incorrectly describes the denominator of the 15.45% supervisor-overhead share, this localized inconsistency does not outweigh the substantial gains in evidence and transparency.
